program_name: SEAS 4.0 — "Sustainable Ship and Shipping 4.0", branded in full as the "Sustainable Ship and Shipping 4.0 Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (SEAS 4.0)". THE PROGRAMME AWARDS A DOUBLE DEGREE, AND EACH AWARDING UNIVERSITY USES ITS OWN LEGAL TITLE. The University of Naples Federico II awards the Italian title "Master interateneo di II livello Sustainable Ship and Shipping 4.0" (inter-university second-level university master); the University of A Coruna awards "Master Universitario Erasmus Mundus en Sostenibilidad e Industria 4.0 aplicada al Sector Maritimo (SEAS 4.0)". Both diplomas carry the joint SEAS 4.0 designation, and UNINA additionally issues a Joint Diploma Supplement in English describing the programme organisation, the student's mobility path and the full transcript of all ECTS obtained. THE ISSUING/COORDINATING INSTITUTION IS UNINA. Consortium (full degree-awarding and teaching partners): University of Naples Federico II (UNINA, Italy — coordinator), Universidade da Coruna (UDC, Spain), Sveuciliste u Zagrebu / University of Zagreb (UNIZG, Croatia), and Technische Universitat Hamburg (TUHH, Germany) as a teaching partner for the third semester. Associated partners named by UNINA include the University of Antwerp, Denmark Technical University, Touro College Berlin, CINECA and Memorial University of Newfoundland, plus "28 aziende ed Enti del settore da sette paesi diversi" (28 companies and classification societies from seven different countries). Programme length 90 ECTS over three semesters (a "year-and-half-long" course, i.e. 1.5 academic years). Academic coordinator at UNINA: Prof. Ermina Begovic, Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale (DII), begovic@unina.it, tel. +39 081 7683708. General mailbox: infomasterseas40@unina.it. THIS IS A STANDALONE PROGRAMME, NOT A CURRICULUM inside an Italian-taught degree — this confirms the research brief's "type: standalone". CRITICAL STATUS FINDING (see uncertainty_notes item 1): the programme was funded by the EU's EACEA "per 4 cicli di studio a partire dal A.A. 2021/22" (for 4 study cycles starting from academic year 2021/22), i.e. intakes 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 only. The programme's own homepage now states "NO Applications for A.Y. 25/26", and the final 2024/25 cohort's graduation ceremony was scheduled for 12 March 2026 in Naples. AS OF 2026-08-30 THERE IS NO OPEN INTAKE AND NO ANNOUNCED RENEWAL.
level: other — this is NOT a Laurea Magistrale and NOT a first-cycle degree. It is an Italian "Master universitario di II livello" (second-level university master), specifically a "Master interateneo di II livello" (inter-university second-level master), which is a post-lauream professional qualification sitting OUTSIDE the Laurea / Laurea Magistrale / Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico system and outside the ministerial degree-class (classe di laurea) framework. This CONFIRMS the research brief's "level: other" and "degree_class: Yok". Structure: 90 ECTS across three semesters (approximately 18 months / 1.5 academic years). Credit distribution per the official Examinations and Award page: "Semester 1 (30 ECTS)", "Semester 2 (30 ECTS)", "Semester 3 (12 ECTS in courses + 18 ECTS in Master Thesis + Internship)" — 30 + 30 + 30 = 90 ECTS. The internship component is quantified as "Internship in the duration of 375 hours" in a company, research centre or a host-university laboratory. Progression is gated: to move from semester 1 to semester 2, and again from semester 2 to semester 3, the student must obtain "a minimum ECTS grade of E (i.e. a pass) in all modules"; "To be awarded the Master Degree, the student must have successfully passed all modules at grade A to E under the ECTS scheme." Each learning activity may be attempted twice; a second failure results in dismissal from the programme. Grading scales differ by host institution: "10 – 30 UNINA, 0-10 UDC, 1-5 UNIZG, 5-1 TUHH", with the ECTS grading scale used in parallel for administrative purposes. The Master Thesis is defended at the University of Naples Federico II. NOTE FOR THE DATASET OWNER: because 90 ECTS post-lauream masters are not part of the Italian bachelor/master degree-class taxonomy used by the rest of this dataset, and because admission requires an already-completed 240-ECTS/4-year qualification rather than a school-leaving certificate or a 180-ECTS bachelor, this item does not map onto the bachelor/master distinction used elsewhere — see uncertainty_notes item 2.
teaching_language: ENGLISH is the language of instruction, examination and application for the whole programme, at all four consortium universities. The programme is described on unina.it as "a year-and-half-long (90 ECTS) integrated, international, innovative course ... taught in English and jointly designed by SEAS 4.0 Consortium Universities", and the application itself is accepted in English only (the 2021/22 UNINA call states applications are to be submitted "in lingua inglese"). All application documents — transcript of records, degree certificate, CV, motivation letter, recommendation letters, personal video — must be in English. [uncertain] THREE QUALIFICATIONS TO THE "100% ENGLISH" CLAIM: (1) ITALIAN IS A COMPULSORY, CREDIT-BEARING COURSE. The official first-semester course list at UNINA includes "Italian language | 3 ECTS" alongside the technical modules. This is a taught Italian-language module inside the curriculum, not merely an optional service course, so a SEAS 4.0 student in Naples takes 3 ECTS of Italian for credit. (2) NATIONAL-LANGUAGE COURSES ARE AN EXPLICIT STUDENT OBLIGATION AT EVERY HOST. The Student Rights and Obligations page requires students to attend national language courses at the host institutions — meaning Italian in Naples, Spanish in Ferrol, and Croatian or German in semester 3 depending on the mobility choice. This is a duty, not an offer. (3) NO unina.it PAGE STATES THE LANGUAGE OF THE THIRD-SEMESTER COURSES HOSTED AT UNIZG AND TUHH. The Courses-by-semester page lists them only under institutional abbreviations with English titles (UNIZG: Ship Structural Design, Advanced Structural Analysis, Fundamentals of Ship Vibration, Multi-Criteria Design and Optimization; TUHH: Innovative CFD Approaches, Arctic Technology) and carries no language statement at all. Since the whole programme is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, English delivery at the partners is the near-certain intent, but it is not stated in writing on any unina.it source. NOTE ALSO A CREDIT-COUNT INCONSISTENCY IN THE PUBLISHED COURSE LIST (see uncertainty_notes item 6): the semester-1 list at UNINA sums to 39 ECTS and the semester-2 list at UDC to 42 ECTS, while the Examinations and Award page fixes each semester at 30 ECTS — so part of each list must be elective, but no unina.it page says which modules are compulsory and which are choices.
campus: [uncertain] MULTI-COUNTRY MOBILITY PROGRAMME — THERE IS NO SINGLE CAMPUS, and the Naples teaching venue is not stated precisely on any unina.it page. THE MOBILITY PATH IS FIXED FOR SEMESTERS 1 AND 2 AND CHOSEN FOR SEMESTER 3: — SEMESTER 1 (September–December): NAPLES, University of Naples Federico II. — SEMESTER 2 (February–May): FERROL, SPAIN, Universidade da Coruna, Escuela Politecnica Superior, Mendizabal s/n, 15403 Ferrol. — SEMESTER 3 (from September): student's choice of ONE of the four consortium universities — UNINA (Naples), UDC (Ferrol), UNIZG (University of Zagreb, Fakultet strojarstva i brodogradnje, Ivana Lucica 5, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia) or TUHH (Technische Universitat Hamburg, Institut fur Konstruktion und Festigkeit von Schiffen, Am Schwarzenberg-Campus 4C, 21073 Hamburg, Germany). — INTERNSHIP AND THESIS (375 hours, more than three months): in a company, research centre or a host-university laboratory, location not fixed. — THESIS DEFENCE: always back in NAPLES at UNINA, scheduled by the academic calendar for early March (Intake 2023/24: 3–4 March 2025; Intake 2024/25: 9–10 March 2026). WHAT IS ACTUALLY DOCUMENTED FOR NAPLES: every unina.it source gives only the ADMINISTRATIVE address of the coordinating department — "Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale, Via Claudio 21, 80125 Napoli (Italy)" (the DII/Fuorigrotta engineering area of Federico II, the same complex as Piazzale Tecchio). NO unina.it page names the lecture rooms or the specific building used for SEAS 4.0 teaching, so "Via Claudio 21" should be read as the department contact point rather than as a verified classroom location. ONE CEREMONIAL VENUE IS DOCUMENTED AND IS A DIFFERENT SITE: the 2024/25 graduation ceremony of 12 March 2026 was announced for "Aula De Sanctis, Corso Umberto I 40" — the University's historic central headquarters on Corso Umberto I, not the engineering campus. RELATIVE TO THE CAMPUS LIST IN THIS DATASET'S FIELD DEFINITION: the Naples component belongs to the Fuorigrotta / Via Claudio–Piazzale Tecchio engineering area, and is NOT Monte Sant'Angelo, Policlinico, Portici, San Giovanni a Teduccio or Frullone. Administrative registration is centralised at the coordinator's institution: "registration always takes place administratively at the Coordinator's institution" (UNINA), and "Enrolment at UNINA" was scheduled for 9 September 2024 for the last intake, immediately before the UNINA Welcome Week of 9–13 September 2024.
degree_class: NONE — there is no Italian degree class (classe di laurea) code for this qualification, and this CONFIRMS the research brief's "degree_class: Yok". Degree classes (L-xx for first-cycle Laurea, LM-xx for second-cycle Laurea Magistrale, LM-xx c.u. for single-cycle) are assigned by ministerial decree only to Laurea and Laurea Magistrale programmes. A "Master universitario di II livello" under art. 3 comma 9 of D.M. 270/2004 is a post-lauream professional qualification with no degree class, no ministerial class code, and no automatic access to the Italian public-competition career tracks that a Laurea Magistrale opens. Consequently: (a) SEAS 4.0 does NOT appear in the University's degree-programme catalogue (corsi di studio) or on the orientation portal orientamento.unina.it alongside the Laurea/Laurea Magistrale courses; it belongs to the separate "Master di I e II livello" post-laurea catalogue; (b) it is administered by the Department of Industrial Engineering (DII) within the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base area, but no "area didattica" degree-class record exists for it. WHAT REPLACES THE DEGREE CLASS AS THE FORMAL DESIGNATION: the Italian legal title "Master interateneo di II livello Sustainable Ship and Shipping 4.0", the Spanish legal title "Master Universitario Erasmus Mundus en Sostenibilidad e Industria 4.0 aplicada al Sector Maritimo (SEAS 4.0)", and the joint European designation "Sustainable Ship and Shipping 4.0 Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (SEAS 4.0)", supported by a UNINA-issued Joint Diploma Supplement in English.
admission_type: SELECTION CALL — a competitive, consortium-run international selection, NOT open access, NOT TOLC, NOT SAT, and NOT the Italian numero-programmato/graduatoria system used for Federico II's restricted-access degrees. There is no bando di ammissione published in the University's numero-programmato bandi index; the call is issued by the SEAS 4.0 Consortium and hosted on the programme's own unina.it subdomain, and was relayed as a news item by unina.it and by the DII. THE PROCEDURE IS A TWO-STAGE, 100-POINT COMPETITIVE SELECTION: STAGE 1 — documentary evaluation of the online application by the Education Board, scored out of 75 points on five criteria (academic performance from GPA and transcripts 0–30; academic references from two recommendation letters 0–10; language level from language certificates 0–5; motivation and fit from the motivation letter 0–15; multicultural learning from the personal video 0–10). Candidates scoring below 50 points are not invited to interview. STAGE 2 — an interview of "maximum 20 minutes duration" worth a further 25 points (academic performance 0–15, language level 0–5, motivation and fit 0–10). RANKING AND OUTCOME: "Applicants obtaining a 70/100 minimum score will be ranked and divided into MAIN LIST and RESERVE LIST." MAIN LIST candidates are offered the Erasmus Mundus scholarships; RESERVE LIST candidates receive a scholarship only if a main-list candidate declines, and may otherwise enrol as SELF-FUNDED students by paying the participation costs. Candidates not selected may also apply as self-funded students. THERE IS A HARD NATIONALITY DIVERSITY CAP: "No more than three students from the same nationality can be selected in the main list." ADDITIONAL CONSORTIUM POLICY: the selection promotes gender balance, supports applicants with disabilities (a "Special needs evidence" document may be uploaded) and welcomes lifelong-learning applicants; there is no age limit ("No, there is not"). AN APPEALS ROUTE EXISTS (dedicated Appeals page on the programme site). NO ITALIAN-SIDE ENTRANCE COMPETITION APPLIES: unlike Federico II's numero-programmato degrees, there is no unina.it-run written admission test and no Italian graduatoria; the ranking is produced by the Education Board of the four-university consortium. ONE APPLICATION, NO AMENDMENTS: "once submitted the application cannot be amended." CURRENT STATUS AS OF 2026-08-30: NO SELECTION IS RUNNING. The homepage states "NO Applications for A.Y. 25/26" and the online application form page is still frozen at "Application form 2024-2025 ... deadline 15 march 2024".
academic_requirements: [uncertain] A COMPLETED HIGHER-EDUCATION QUALIFICATION WORTH AT LEAST 240 ECTS (i.e. at least four years of university study) IN A RELEVANT TECHNICAL FIELD. Exact wording on the Admission Requirements page: "The Programme is open to APPLICANTS who hold 240 ECTS or equivalent" in the following fields — "Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering", "Maritime Engineering", "Nautical and Maritime Transport", "Mechanical Engineering", "Civil Engineering", "Aerospace Engineering", "Electrical Engineering", "Electric Power Engineering", "Electronic Engineering", "Applied Mathematics", "Physics". OTHER TECHNICAL DISCIPLINES ARE NOT EXCLUDED BUT ARE DISCRETIONARY: "Applicants holding at least 240 ECTS in other technical disciplines can apply and their admission will be considered by Education Board." The FAQ restates the credit rule in years: "Applicants must have at least 4 years of bachelor studies." NO MINIMUM GRADE THRESHOLD IS PUBLISHED — unlike several Federico II master's degrees, SEAS 4.0 publishes no minimum GPA or minimum degree mark; instead the GPA feeds the competitive score (0–30 points from "GPA and student transcripts", plus 0–15 at interview). NO SUBJECT-BY-SUBJECT CFU/ECTS BREAKDOWN is required — there is no "at least X ECTS in mathematics" style rule of the kind used by UNINA's Laurea Magistrale programmes; the 240-ECTS total plus the field list is the whole academic gate. NO AGE LIMIT: FAQ — "No, there is not." WHY THIS FIELD IS MARKED UNCERTAIN — A REAL LEGAL TENSION: Italian law admits candidates to a "Master universitario di II livello" only if they already hold a SECOND-CYCLE degree (Laurea Magistrale / Laurea Specialistica / Laurea vecchio ordinamento) or a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent to one. The SEAS 4.0 consortium requirement, by contrast, is expressed purely as "240 ECTS or equivalent" / "at least 4 years of bachelor studies", which in many non-EU systems is a FOUR-YEAR BACHELOR, i.e. a first-cycle qualification. A holder of a four-year bachelor therefore satisfies the published consortium rule while potentially not satisfying the Italian second-level-master prerequisite. No unina.it page reconciles the two, and the programme's Italian-side enrolment ("registration always takes place administratively at the Coordinator's institution") is where such a mismatch would surface. Any applicant holding a four-year bachelor rather than a master's degree should confirm eligibility in writing with infomasterseas40@unina.it / begovic@unina.it before applying. SECOND POINT: the transcript and degree certificate must be submitted as CERTIFIED COPIES IN ENGLISH, stating "credits, average grade and workload" — an applicant whose institution issues no English transcript must arrange certified translation before applying.
entry_exam_or_test: NO WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAM, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT, NO PORTFOLIO — but THERE IS A COMPULSORY INTERVIEW AND A COMPULSORY VIDEO SUBMISSION, which is unusual for a Federico II programme and is the distinguishing feature of this admission. THE THREE ASSESSED COMPONENTS ARE: (1) DOCUMENTARY EVALUATION of the online application by the SEAS 4.0 Education Board — scored 0–75 across GPA/transcripts, two recommendation letters, language certificate, motivation letter and the personal video. Candidates scoring below 50 in this stage are not invited to interview. (2) A PERSONAL VIDEO, uploaded as a downloadable link at application time: "A link to a downloadable personal video in which you should address your prior experiences and motivations. The video must not exceed five (5) minutes." It is scored 0–10 under the criterion "Multicultural learning". THIS IS A HARD APPLICATION REQUIREMENT, NOT AN OPTION. (3) AN INTERVIEW: "The selected candidates are invited to the interview of maximum 20 minutes duration", worth 0–25 points (academic performance 0–15, language level 0–5, motivation and fit 0–10). The interview doubles as the de facto oral English check. FINAL GATE: a combined score of at least 70/100 is required to be ranked at all — below 70 the candidate is neither on the main list nor on the reserve list. THE ENGLISH REQUIREMENT IS SATISFIED BY CERTIFICATE, NOT BY A TEST SAT AT UNINA (see language_requirements), although the certificate score feeds directly into the 0–5 documentary points and the 0–5 interview points. NO ITALIAN-LANGUAGE ENTRANCE TEST APPLIES AT ADMISSION; Italian is instead taught inside the programme as a 3-ECTS first-semester module. NO UNIVERSITALY/MINISTERIAL ADMISSION TEST APPLIES either — for non-EU applicants the Universitaly step is a visa/pre-enrolment formality performed AFTER admission, using the consortium's Letter of Admission, not a competitive test.
seats_total: [uncertain] NO TOTAL SEAT NUMBER IS PUBLISHED ON ANY unina.it PAGE — the programme publishes a scholarship count, not a cohort cap, and adds an unquantified number of self-funded places. WHAT IS PUBLISHED: "22 Erasmus Mundus scholarships (19 from partner countries and 3 from programme countries)" on the programme homepage, matched by the 2021/22 UNINA call announcement "22 borse di studio Erasmus Mundus", plus "Additional Places: limited self-financed positions available" (the Italian call speaks of a limited number of self-funded places, without a figure). THE ONE HARD COHORT FIGURE FOUND ON unina.it IS OBSERVATIONAL, NOT A QUOTA: the University's own video news item on the first cycle reports "21 studenti giunti da 14 paesi diversi di tutto il mondo" (21 students from 14 different countries) completing the first semester — i.e. an actual cohort of about 21 for the 2021/22 intake, consistent with the 22 scholarships. WHY THIS IS UNCERTAIN: it is NOT stated anywhere on unina.it whether the figure of 22 is PER INTAKE or the TOTAL for the whole four-cycle EACEA project. Both readings are defensible — the phrasing on the homepage and in the 2021/22 call is bare ("22 Erasmus Mundus scholarships") with no "per year" or "per intake" qualifier, while the 21-student first cohort points towards a per-intake reading for at least the first cycle. A DIFFERENT KIND OF CAP IS EXPLICIT AND BINDING: "No more than three students from the same nationality can be selected in the main list" — a diversity ceiling that functions as a per-nationality seat limit regardless of the total. PRACTICAL NOTE: because the ranking uses a fixed 70/100 quality threshold rather than a fixed number of places, the effective cohort size in any cycle is the number of scholarships plus however many 70+ candidates chose to self-fund. AS OF 2026-08-30 THE QUESTION IS MOOT: no intake is open, so no seat figure is current.
non_eu_reserved_seats: [uncertain] THE ITALIAN CONCEPT OF A RESERVED NON-EU QUOTA DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS PROGRAMME, AND NO SUCH FIGURE IS PUBLISHED. Federico II reserves numbered seats for non-EU citizens residing abroad only in its numero-programmato degree programmes; SEAS 4.0 is a post-lauream Master universitario recruited through a consortium call, so it has no Italian-style riserva. WHAT EXISTS INSTEAD IS AN ERASMUS-MUNDUS NATIONALITY SPLIT OF THE SCHOLARSHIPS, which is the closest available proxy: of the "22 Erasmus Mundus scholarships", "19 from partner countries and 3 from programme countries". In Erasmus Mundus terminology a PROGRAMME COUNTRY is an EU Member State or an associated country participating in the Erasmus+ programme, and a PARTNER COUNTRY is any other country in the world; "Partner country" therefore maps approximately, but NOT exactly, onto "non-EU". On that reading roughly 19 of 22 funded places (about 86%) were earmarked for applicants from outside the Erasmus+ programme countries — an unusually non-EU-weighted allocation compared with a typical Federico II degree, and the mirror image of the Italian system where non-EU applicants get the small reserved slice. TWO CAVEATS THAT MAKE THIS FIELD UNCERTAIN: (1) the 22/19/3 split is stated without the qualifier "per intake" or "in total" (see seats_total), so the annual non-EU figure cannot be asserted with confidence; (2) the Programme/Partner-country distinction is defined by RESIDENCE and the Erasmus+ country list, not by citizenship or by the EU/non-EU line used elsewhere in this dataset — the entry-level document "Proof of place of residence (accepted documents are indicated in the PRADO website)" exists precisely to establish which category an applicant falls into, and the Declaration of Honour is supplied in two versions, "Programme or Partner Countries Applicant version". SELF-FUNDED PLACES CARRY NO NATIONALITY QUOTA AT ALL, only the differentiated participation cost (4500 EUR/year for programme-country applicants, 9000 EUR/year for partner-country applicants) and the three-per-nationality main-list cap.
language_requirements: [uncertain] ENGLISH AT CEFR B2 OR ABOVE IS THE ONLY ADMISSION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT; NO ITALIAN IS REQUIRED TO BE ADMITTED. THE STRICT, NUMERIC VERSION (Admission Requirements page) — applicants must have "at least B2 level of English-language proficiency according to the Common European Framework", evidenced by one of: "6 IELTS with at least 5.0 point in each section"; "TOEFL (paper based) at least 550 points with 4.5 in the writing section"; "TOEFL (IBT) 79 points with at least 17 points in every section". Note the sub-score floors — an overall IELTS 6.0 with a 4.5 in one band does NOT satisfy the rule, and an iBT 79 with a 16 in one section does not either. THE LOOSER VERSION, AND THIS IS THE CONFLICT — the FAQ page states: "The requested English level is at least B2. The valid certificates are: IELTS, TOFEL, a document from the university, or a certificate of previous studies in English language." That admits a university-issued medium-of-instruction letter, which the Admission Requirements page does not mention at all. The Visas page supports the looser reading for the visa stage: the language certificate is "not required if you are English native speaker or your previous studies were held in English". SO TWO OFFICIAL PAGES ON THE SAME unina.it SITE GIVE DIFFERENT ANSWERS to the single most common applicant question — whether an English-medium-of-instruction letter replaces IELTS/TOEFL. Since the language certificate is also SCORED in the competitive selection (0–5 points on documents, 0–5 at interview), an applicant relying on a university letter risks scoring zero on a criterion where a certified IELTS/TOEFL scores full marks, even if the letter is technically accepted. RECOMMENDATION: obtain IELTS/TOEFL at the stated thresholds and confirm any substitute with infomasterseas40@unina.it. ITALIAN — NOT AN ADMISSION REQUIREMENT, BUT COMPULSORY INSIDE THE PROGRAMME. No Italian certificate and no Italian test is needed to apply, to be admitted, or for the visa. However: (a) the first semester at UNINA includes a credit-bearing "Italian language | 3 ECTS" module in the official course list; (b) the Student Rights and Obligations page requires students to attend the national language courses at the host institutions, i.e. Italian in Naples and Spanish in Ferrol, and Croatian or German in semester 3 depending on the mobility choice. So Italian is a graduation-side, not an admission-side, requirement — and unlike several UNINA degrees, here it is delivered as a taught module rather than as a certificate to be obtained from the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo. LANGUAGE OF THE APPLICATION AND OF THE DOCUMENTS: English only. The transcript of records and the highest degree certificate must be submitted as "Certified copy ... (in English)", the CV in Europass format, the motivation letter, the two recommendation letters and the max-5-minute personal video all in English.
application_deadline_eu: [uncertain] THERE IS NO SEPARATE EU DEADLINE — the SEAS 4.0 consortium runs ONE single application window with ONE deadline for all applicants worldwide, EU and non-EU alike. The Programme/Partner-country distinction affects the scholarship allocation and the participation cost, NOT the calendar. AND, CRITICALLY, THERE IS NO CURRENT DEADLINE AT ALL: the programme homepage states "NO Applications for A.Y. 25/26", the four EACEA-funded cycles (2021/22 through 2024/25) are complete, and no 2026/27 call has been published on any unina.it page as of 2026-08-30. THE LAST PUBLISHED CYCLE — INTAKE 2024/25 (page still online, headed "Important Dates – INTAKE 2024/25"): — 2024-03-15: "Application submission deadline: 15th March 2024"; — 2024-03-31: non-eligible and non-selected applicants notified by e-mail, and ranked applicants (70/100 or above) informed of their main-list or reserve-list position ("Applicants obtaining a 70/100 minimum score, are ranked and divided into MAIN LIST and RESERVE LIST and informed by email before March 31st"); — 2024-04-15: "Notification to candidates on selection process results: 15th April 2024"; — 2024-05-15: "Deadline for confirmation on scholarship acceptance: 15th May 2024"; — 2024-09-09: "Enrolment at UNINA: 9th September 2024"; — 2024-09-09 to 2024-09-13: "Welcome Week: 9th – 13th September 2024"; — 2024-09-16 to 2024-12-20: "First semester didactic activities: 16th September – 20th December"; — January 2025: first exam session at UNINA (8 January – 6 February 2025 per the academic calendar). THE FIRST-EVER CYCLE, FOR COMPARISON — A.Y. 2021/22, announced by unina.it: applications open "dal 1 dicembre 2020 al 1 marzo 2021" (1 December 2020 to 1 March 2021). PATTERN: a roughly three-month winter window closing at the start of March, results in April, scholarship acceptance by mid-May, enrolment and Welcome Week in the second week of September. Anyone hoping for a revived intake should watch https://www.master-seas40.unina.it/application-and-admission/important-dates/ and https://www.international.unina.it/opportunities/call-for-applicants/ from about November onwards, and should write to infomasterseas40@unina.it to ask whether the programme has been re-funded. MARKED UNCERTAIN because every date above is historical: none of them is an actionable deadline for a prospective 2026/27 or 2027/28 applicant.
application_deadline_non_eu: [uncertain] IDENTICAL TO THE EU DEADLINE FOR THE ADMISSION STEP — the consortium publishes one deadline for everyone (last published: 15 March 2024 for Intake 2024/25; 1 March 2021 for the first cycle), with no earlier cut-off for non-EU applicants. AND AGAIN, THERE IS NO CURRENT INTAKE: "NO Applications for A.Y. 25/26", four EACEA cycles completed, no announced renewal as of 2026-08-30. WHERE NON-EU APPLICANTS DO FACE AN EXTRA, LATER PIPELINE: after being admitted by the consortium, a non-EU applicant residing abroad must obtain an Italian type-D study visa through the ministerial UNIVERSITALY portal. The programme's Visas page states: "Requesting D Type visa for study in Italy has to be done through the UNIVERSITALY web platform where you will indicate University of Naples Federico II as host institution and EMJMD SEAS 4.0." Note the sequencing — the consortium's Letter of Admission is an input to the Universitaly application, so the visa step FOLLOWS admission and does not compete with it. THE UNIVERSITY-WIDE UNIVERSITALY CALENDAR THAT WOULD APPLY (a.y. 2026/2027, from international.unina.it): 15 June 2026 pre-enrolment application deadline to Federico II, after which "no programme changes are permitted" and pre-enrolment remains open only for restricted-access programmes; then the visa application at the Italian Embassy/Consulate; then completion of enrolment in Naples. IMPORTANT MISMATCH TO BE AWARE OF: those university-wide dates are written for degree programmes (Laurea, Laurea Magistrale, single-cycle) and were built around a September start, whereas the SEAS 4.0 consortium's own calendar admits candidates in April and enrols them at UNINA on the second Monday of September. In the four completed cycles the consortium timetable, not the Universitaly calendar, was the operative one for admission; Universitaly served only the visa. NO unina.it PAGE STATES HOW THE TWO CALENDARS INTERACT FOR THIS SPECIFIC MASTER — hence the [uncertain] mark. VISA RESPONSIBILITY IS EXPLICITLY THE STUDENT'S: FAQ — "You are entirely responsible for completing your visa request and for obtaining it before the start of your studies." Non-EU applicants should therefore budget at least three to four months between the April admission notification and the September enrolment date for the visa, and should note that the passport must be "valid at least for other 3 months after the planned date of exit from Schengen Area".
required_documents: THE CONSORTIUM PUBLISHES A COMPLETE, PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC CHECKLIST (unusual for a Federico II programme — most refer applicants to university-level pages). ALL ITEMS ARE UPLOADED AS PDF TO THE ONLINE APPLICATION FORM, AND "once submitted the application cannot be amended." THE TWELVE ITEMS, VERBATIM: (1) "Proof of place of residence (accepted documents are indicated in the PRADO website)" — this establishes whether you count as a Programme-country or Partner-country applicant, which determines both your scholarship pool and your participation cost, so it is not a formality; (2) "Copy of the ID/ passport (passport will be required for NON EU students)"; (3) "Certified copy of the transcript of records of all courses (in English)"; (4) "Certified copy of the highest degree obtained, stating credits, average grade and workload (in English)" — note the three data points the certificate must itself show: credits, average grade, workload; (5) "Copy of Language Certificate"; (6) "Full curriculum vitae in Europass format" — the Europass template is mandatory, not suggested; (7) "Letter of motivation to participate in the SEAS 4.0 Programme" (scored 0–15 on documents and 0–10 at interview); (8) "Recommendation letters from two referees" (scored 0–10; two letters, labelled A and B in the scoring grid); (9) a Declaration of Honour, supplied in two versions — "Programme or Partner Countries Applicant version" — of which you sign the one matching your residence; (10) "A link to a downloadable personal video in which you should address your prior experiences and motivations. The video must not exceed five (5) minutes." (scored 0–10 under "Multicultural learning"; the link must be DOWNLOADABLE, not merely viewable); (11) "Special needs evidence" — for applicants requesting disability support; (12) "Any supplementary information that may be consider relevant by the Applicant". LANGUAGE AND CERTIFICATION RULES: the transcript and the degree certificate must be CERTIFIED COPIES and must be IN ENGLISH — applicants whose institution issues documents in another language must arrange certified translation before applying. No application fee is mentioned on any page. SEPARATE, LATER DOCUMENT SET FOR THE NON-EU VISA (Universitaly step C, from the programme's Visas page): "Your passport, the document has to be valid at least for other 3 months after the planned date of exit from Schengen Area"; the Letter of Admission issued by the consortium; proof of place of residence; "Certified copy of the transcript of records of all courses (in English) and of the highest degree obtained"; "Copy of Language Certificate (not required if you are English native speaker or your previous studies were held in English)". AT THE EMBASSY, ADDITIONALLY: the visa request form, flight booking and accommodation reservation, and financial proof — either the scholarship documentation or "bank statement of your current account giving your personal details and the details of the Bank"; if the account is not the applicant's own, "they need to attach a declaration to their bank statement, stating that they consent to your use of their current account (affidavit)". NOTE ON QUALIFICATION RECOGNITION: the university-wide rule for non-EU applicants requires a "Declaration of value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained or certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres" (CIMEA in Italy). The SEAS 4.0 pages do NOT list the Declaration of Value or CIMEA statements among the application documents — but since final registration is administrative at UNINA, an admitted non-EU student should expect to produce them at enrolment; confirm with infomasterseas40@unina.it. FINALLY, A SIGNED STUDENT AGREEMENT is required after admission: students sign an agreement "defining rights and duties", and "Enrolment is only official after paying the tuition fee to the account of the Consortium."
tuition_or_fees_link: [uncertain] THIS MASTER IS NOT COVERED BY FEDERICO II'S ORDINARY STUDENT-CONTRIBUTION SYSTEM. Because it is a post-lauream Master universitario run by an international consortium, the ISEEU-based contribution bands, the non-EU total exemption and the flat 200 EUR EU-citizen rule that apply to Federico II's Laurea and Laurea Magistrale programmes DO NOT APPLY here; instead the consortium charges a flat "participation cost" that is paid to the consortium's own account. THE PUBLISHED FIGURES (programme homepage): "Programme country applicants: 4500 € / year" and "Partner country applicants: 9000 € / year". PAYMENT AND ENROLMENT: "Enrolment is only official after paying the tuition fee to the account of the Consortium", and "registration always takes place administratively at the Coordinator's institution" (UNINA). WHY MARKED UNCERTAIN — TWO GENUINE AMBIGUITIES: (1) THE PROGRAMME LASTS 1.5 YEARS BUT THE FEE IS QUOTED PER YEAR, and no unina.it page states the total payable. Read literally, a self-funded programme-country student would owe about 6,750 EUR and a partner-country student about 13,500 EUR over three semesters; read as two annual instalments, 9,000 EUR and 18,000 EUR. No page resolves this, and no payment schedule or instalment plan is published anywhere on unina.it. (2) NO unina.it FEE PAGE EXISTS FOR THIS MASTER — the figures appear only in a summary block on the programme homepage; the Students Grants page and the Student Rights page both discuss the fee without giving a number, and SEAS 4.0 does not appear in the University's "Master di I e II livello" fee/bando catalogue. FOR SCHOLARSHIP HOLDERS THE FEE IS ZERO: the Erasmus Mundus scholarship "covers tuition fees, participation costs, contribution to travel and installation costs, and monthly allowance" — more precisely "the students' participation costs (including the tuition fees, full insurance coverage and any other mandatory costs)", "a contribution to student travel and installation cost" and "a subsistence allowance for the entire duration of the SEAS 4.0 Master's programme". THE SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS, from the FAQ: "the monthly living allowance of 1000 €/month for all scholarship holders"; travel "1000 €/year for a scholarship holder residing in a Programme country", "2000 €/year for a scholarship holder residing in a Partner country less than 4000 km from the EMJMD coordinating institution", "3000 €/year for a scholarship holder residing in a Partner country 4000 km or more"; settling-in "1000 €, for scholarship holders residing in a Partner country only". TWO ALLOWANCE RESTRICTIONS: "scholarship holders studying in their country of residence will not receive the subsistence allowance during that period", and "a scholarship holder from a Partner country cannot receive the subsistence allowance for more than 3 months when studying in any Partner country". NO OTHER FUNDING IS OFFERED: the Additional Funding page states plainly "At the moment no additional funding is available", while the Students Grants page says the consortium is "seeking for additional funding sources available for SEAS 4.0 students" whose eligibility "may depend on factors including nationality and residency status". RELEVANT LINKS: programme cost summary — https://www.master-seas40.unina.it/ ; scholarship terms — https://www.master-seas40.unina.it/scholarship/students-grants/emjdm/ ; FAQ with the allowance figures — https://www.master-seas40.unina.it/about-seas-4-0/faq/ ; additional funding — https://www.master-seas40.unina.it/scholarship/students-grants/additional-funding/ ; general Federico II fees hub (NOT applicable to this master, listed only for completeness) — https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse . AS OF 2026-08-30 all of these figures are historical, since no intake is open.

uncertainty_notes: 1) *** THE PROGRAMME IS DORMANT — THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING AND IT OUTRANKS EVERY OTHER FIELD. *** The EACEA funded SEAS 4.0 "per 4 cicli di studio a partire dal A.A. 2021/22" (for four study cycles from 2021/22), i.e. intakes 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25. All four have been consumed. The programme homepage states "NO Applications for A.Y. 25/26"; the online application form is frozen at "Application form 2024-2025 ... deadline 15 march 2024"; the Important Dates page is still headed "Important Dates – INTAKE 2024/25"; the Academic Calendar covers only Intakes 2023/24 and 2024/25; international.unina.it lists SEAS 4.0 among ARCHIVED calls; and SEAS 4.0 does NOT appear in Federico II's current "Master di I e II livello" catalogue at https://www.unina.it/didattica/post-laurea/master alongside the 2024/25–2026/27 offerings. The last cohort's thesis defence (9–10 March 2026) and graduation ceremony (12 March 2026, Aula De Sanctis, Corso Umberto I 40) are the final scheduled events. NO unina.it PAGE EXPLICITLY SAYS THE PROGRAMME IS DISCONTINUED, and the website is still maintained (copyright notice updated to 2026), so a re-funded fifth cycle is not impossible — but as of 2026-08-30 there is no open intake, no 2026/27 call, and no announced renewal. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DATASET: every deadline, fee and seat figure recorded here is HISTORICAL. Do not present SEAS 4.0 to a prospective applicant as an available option without first writing to infomasterseas40@unina.it / begovic@unina.it to ask whether the programme has been re-funded. 2) *** TENTATIVE ITEM — INCLUSION IN THIS DATASET IS PENDING CONFIRMATION, AS FLAGGED IN THE RESEARCH BRIEF. *** SEAS 4.0 is a "Master interateneo di II livello", an Italian post-lauream professional university master governed by art. 3 comma 9 of D.M. 270/2004. It sits entirely OUTSIDE the Laurea / Laurea Magistrale / Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico system that the rest of this dataset describes: it has no degree class (no L-xx or LM-xx code), it is 90 ECTS rather than 180 or 120, it lasts 1.5 years rather than 3 or 2, it is not listed in the University's corsi di studio catalogue or on orientamento.unina.it, it does not confer the legal effects of a Laurea Magistrale in Italy, and it does not qualify a graduate for the Italian state professional examinations or public-competition tracks that an LM opens. Its admission gate is also structurally different: it presupposes a COMPLETED 240-ECTS qualification (i.e. it is a post-master or post-4-year-bachelor top-up), so it is neither a "bachelor admission" nor a "master admission" in the sense used by the other 30 records in this folder. RECOMMENDATION: treat this record as a separate "other / post-graduate professional master" category, or exclude it, but do NOT merge it into the bachelor/master admission-requirements comparison tables without a category flag — the fee model, the deadline model, the seat model and the qualification model are all different from every other item in the set. 3) MINIMUM ENTRY QUALIFICATION — POSSIBLE LEGAL MISMATCH. The consortium requires "240 ECTS or equivalent" / "at least 4 years of bachelor studies", which in many non-EU systems is a FIRST-cycle four-year bachelor. Italian law admits candidates to a Master universitario di II livello only if they hold a SECOND-cycle degree (Laurea Magistrale/Specialistica or equivalent). Since final registration is administrative at UNINA, a four-year-bachelor holder could satisfy the published consortium rule yet face an Italian-side eligibility question. No unina.it page addresses this. Confirm in writing before applying. 4) ENGLISH-CERTIFICATE RULE — TWO OFFICIAL PAGES DISAGREE. The Admission Requirements page gives a strict numeric list (IELTS 6.0 with 5.0 in every band; TOEFL paper 550 with 4.5 writing; TOEFL iBT 79 with 17 in every section). The FAQ page additionally accepts "a document from the university, or a certificate of previous studies in English language", and the Visas page waives the certificate for native speakers and for those whose previous studies were in English. Assume the strict list is binding for the competitive score (the certificate is worth up to 5 documentary points plus 5 interview points) and treat the FAQ wording as a possible discretionary fallback only. 5) NO SEAT CAP IS PUBLISHED, AND THE "22 SCHOLARSHIPS" FIGURE IS AMBIGUOUS. Neither the homepage nor the 2021/22 call states whether 22 (19 partner-country + 3 programme-country) is PER INTAKE or the TOTAL across the four cycles. The observed first cohort of "21 studenti giunti da 14 paesi diversi" supports a per-intake reading for at least cycle 1, but this is inference, not a published statement. Separately, the number of self-funded places is never quantified — only "limited". The one hard, published cap is the diversity rule: "No more than three students from the same nationality can be selected in the main list." 6) PUBLISHED COURSE LISTS DO NOT ADD UP TO THE PUBLISHED SEMESTER CREDITS. The Examinations and Award page fixes Semester 1 and Semester 2 at 30 ECTS each, but the Courses-by-semester page lists modules summing to 39 ECTS in semester 1 at UNINA (Regulatory Framework for Maritime Industry 4.0 3; Ship Design 6; Alternative Fuels For Shipping 3; 2nd Generation Stability Criteria 3; Structural Analysis of Ships and Offshore Structures 6; Virtual Prototyping 6; Robotics & Underwater Robotics 6; Ship Seakeeping 3; Italian language 3) and 42 ECTS in semester 2 at UDC (Industry 4.0 Enabling Technologies 6; Industrial Internet of Things 6; Statistical models for marine technology innovation 6; Autonomous (marine) vehicles 6; Introduction to marine Computational Fluid Dynamics 6; Manoeuvrability and Shallow Water Ship Hydrodynamics 3; Ship Operations & Decision Support Systems 6; Transport economics 3). Some modules must therefore be elective, but NO unina.it page says which are compulsory and which are choices — and the FAQ's blunt "No, all mandatory courses are MANDATORY" does not resolve it. Do not present either list as a fixed 30-ECTS curriculum. 7) THE NAPLES TEACHING VENUE IS NOT DOCUMENTED. Every unina.it source gives only the coordinating department's administrative address, "Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale, Via Claudio 21, 80125 Napoli" (the Fuorigrotta engineering area). No lecture-room or building is named for SEAS 4.0 teaching, and the only ceremonial venue documented — Aula De Sanctis, Corso Umberto I 40 — is the University's historic central headquarters, a different site. Treat "Via Claudio 21" as a contact point, not a verified classroom. 8) THIRD-SEMESTER TEACHING LANGUAGE AT UNIZG AND TUHH IS NEVER STATED. The Courses-by-semester page lists those modules only by institutional abbreviation with English titles and carries no language declaration. English delivery is the near-certain intent of an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, but it is not written down on any unina.it page. 9) FEE TOTAL IS UNRESOLVED. The participation cost is quoted "per year" (4500 EUR programme-country, 9000 EUR partner-country) for a programme that lasts 1.5 years, and no unina.it page gives the total payable, a payment schedule or an instalment plan. Literal pro-rata reading: about 6,750 EUR / 13,500 EUR total. Two-annual-instalment reading: 9,000 EUR / 18,000 EUR. Unresolvable from unina.it. 10) DECLARATION OF VALUE / CIMEA NOT ON THE SEAS 4.0 CHECKLIST. The consortium's 12-item document list omits the Declaration of Value and the CIMEA Statements of Comparability and Verification that Federico II's university-wide international admission regulation requires of non-EU qualification holders. Because registration is administrative at UNINA, an admitted non-EU student should expect to be asked for them at enrolment even though the programme pages do not list them. 11) THE CONSORTIUM CALENDAR AND THE UNIVERSITALY CALENDAR ARE NOT RECONCILED ANYWHERE. The consortium admitted in April and enrolled in early September; Federico II's university-wide non-EU pipeline for degree programmes runs to a 15 June pre-enrolment deadline. No unina.it page explains how the two interlock for this specific master. In the four completed cycles the consortium timetable governed admission and Universitaly served only the visa. 12) DOMAIN/URL PITFALLS FOR ANYONE RE-CHECKING THIS RECORD: the bare hosts master-seas40.unina.it and dii.unina.it DO NOT RESOLVE — the "www." prefix is required.
